brief: The Market Ear compiles twelve charts from multiple banks framing a week of hedge-fund deleveraging, counted down from least to most extreme. Deutsche Bank: tech is underperforming the S&P 500, and systematic/CTA positioning has turned modestly short but stays above prior extremes, leaving room to sell. GS trading desk: S&P futures liquidity (top-of-book depth) is at its lowest since April. Goldman: prime brokerage logs the heaviest single-stock shorting week since June 2022 (about 1.5% of gross market value) and the worst hedge-fund VIP drawdown on record. JPM PI and GS Prime: hedge-fund leverage has fallen to 2018-level extremes, fundamental L/S net leverage at a 1st-percentile 42.3%, beta-adjusted leverage down over 22 points since October to a five-year-low 48.2%, and momentum exposure flipping from +70% to negative. Bespoke: the S&P is 4.10 standard deviations below its 50-day average, the most oversold since 2015. Goldman: short interest (median 3.1%, 90th percentile 8%) has risen toward 2008-2010 peaks, raising squeeze risk. Deutsche Bank's own consolidated positioning gauge sits only at the 11th percentile since 2010, so despite the extremes above, investors are bearish but not at prior extremes, meaning maximum fear may not have been reached yet.
